text:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#12345 - routing-node-heartbeat-threshold (severity: P3). Auto-escalation window 5m.

maria: seeing it too, getting multiple quick pages from the canary group.

aj: acking on PD, pulling up dashboards. link: https://pd.example.com/incidents/12345

pagerduty-bot: maria acknowledged the incident. Dev oncall: aj assigned.

aj: quick check — dashboards show a ~30s spike in router latency for canary-traffic only. No error budget burn, no 5xx spike.

devon: logs look noisy from router-12 in us-west-2, lots of short-lived conn churn around same timestamps.

aj: running a quick targeted query for conn resets:
```bash
kubectl logs router-12 -n infra --since=2m | grep -E "RST|reset|conn close" | tail -n 50
```

aj: output shows a burst of `RST` from ephemeral proxy reconnects. Could be a transient infra flap or backend health check jitter.

maria: Incidentbot shows 3 pages in last 2m and then one auto-resolve. Pager had auto-resolve enabled for transient spikes — might be a dup.

incidentbot: PagerDuty auto-resolved incident PD#12345 after 4m 12s (no ack escalation).

aj: interesting — PD auto-resolved but slack notifications still streamed. Looks like oncall saw it live though. No customer-facing errors in error-rate dashboard.

sre-watch: noticed metric tagging for `canary=true` — traffic pattern shows small ride. Confirming no customer impact based on API gateway 5xx and latency across production (p50/p95) = normal.

maria: I'm going to mute the specific canary alert rule temporarily and open a follow-up to tune suppression thresholds. Anyone object?

devon: +1. Also will add router-12 to a quick maintenance check later — possibly noisy NIC/driver.

aj: leaving a quick note in the PD incident (for audit):
"Investigated transient router heartbeat spike affecting canary group only. Cause likely transient proxy/conn churn on router-12. No customer impact. PD auto-resolved. Recommend increasing suppression window for `canary-routing-heartbeat` to 2m and add noise-filter by host jitter."

maria: pinging infra ENG to check router-12 hardware health — @devon can you open a ticket?

devon: opened INF-789, added logs and timestamps. Will run NIC diagnostics this afternoon.

aj: marking this thread as "no impact, auto-resolved" and moving to follow-up lane. If PD re-fires, we keep normal oncall flow. :white_check_mark:

incidentbot: Thread closed by aj.

maria: thanks all — good quick triage.

sre-watch: logging action items: [INF-789], update alert suppression, add host jitter metric to canary rule.

aj: last_message_ts set to 7952104680.
